Prose:
The heavy tread of boots echoed from the corridor outside, approaching the gate that separated the stone-walled pen from the world beyond. A guard stepped forward, his presence casting a long, distorted shadow across the huddled captives. He shifted his weight, the metal staff he carried clattering against the rough-hewn floor with a rhythmic, metallic *tap-tap-tap* that seemed to count out the seconds of their suffering. His gaze was glazed with boredom, scanning the faces of the thirty souls inside not with malice, but with the detached appraisal of a man checking livestock before an auction.

The masked man in purple stood near the crate, flipping another page of his ledger. The black tip of his cane tapped in sync with the guard’s footsteps, a metronome keeping time for a performance of cruelty that the overseer treated as mere administration. He murmured something about the scarred captive, his voice harsh and accented, rolling vowels distorting words Caelen couldn’t parse. *'Evicted,'* Caelen thought, watching the overseer gesture toward the man slumped in the shadows. In this place, status was not a right; it was a lease held at the discretion of those who held the keys.

Caelen forced his chest to rise and fall in shallow, ragged bursts, mimicking the panic-stricken rhythm of the young woman who had been struck earlier. His broad palms rested loosely against the stone wall where his wrists were bound. He focused all his will on keeping his body still, hiding the subtle flex of his arm achieved moments ago. To move now would be to invite a club or a staff blow; stillness was armor.

The guard halted directly in front of Caelen’s cell. The opening yawned between him and the man, a gap filled with the smell of wet stone, unwashed bodies, and something metallic—blood, rust, or fear? He didn't try to name it. The guard’s hand rested casually on the hilt of the blade sheathed at his belt, his fingers loose but ready. Caelen kept his eyes slightly downcast, focusing on a dust mote floating near the floorboards where he had dropped them yesterday, refusing to meet the guard’s vacant gaze.

The man grunted, shifting his staff away from the cell opening and continuing his patrol along the perimeter. With the immediate danger passing, Caelen exhaled slowly, his mind sharpening behind the mask of broken spirit. He mapped the guard’s path: the predictable sweep of the corridor, the brief pause at the gate, the routine inspection of the scarred captive. The lull was short, but it was enough to confirm that while his body felt like lead anchored by this strange, heavy gravity, his mind remained dangerously sharp, waiting for the next opportunity to survive.
